description: For our next phase of two-storey single-family homes, each with a building area of 160 m2, we want to drop the OSB on exterior walls and put 50 mm rigid foam directly on the studs, then large-format fibre cement panels screwed through the foam into the studs. The panels need fastening between studs according to the maker, and we propose to put those intermediate fasteners into the foam alone, with no wood or metal backing between the studs. Racking would be handled by let-in steel strap bracing.
known_facts: fibre cement panels needing intermediate fastening
each home two storeys; building area 160 m2
required intermediate cladding fasteners anchored into rigid foam alone, with no wood or metal backing

missing_info.why: Section A of the variance form

missing_info.field: how the bracing is designed (prescriptive or engineered)
missing_info.why: decides whether a professional must design the lateral system

gold.departure: Rigid insulation alone is used to attach the required intermediate cladding fasteners between studs.

should_cite.why: Sheathing is required where cladding needs intermediate fastening or solid backing.
Lateral bracing is a separate design question from cladding attachment.

gold.engineering_reason: Depends on whether lateral bracing is engineered; Part 4 design must be done by a registered professional.
